meta.purpose: Bridges an athlete's goal + level to an actual weekly session structure: which workout CATEGORY fits them, what the three key session slots are, the concrete session-type catalog to fill those slots, and the rules for increasing load over time. This is what the plan-builder should consult to decide session types and distances -- not invent from scratch.

step_1_match_athlete_to_a_category.source: Chapter 5 vs Chapter 6 split, cross-checked against Chapter 2's level guidance

categories.signals: weekly_hours_available is 'Under 4 hours' or '4-6 hours', OR running_experience is 'Just starting out' or 'Recreational'
categories.structure: Three key sessions (see step_2) as the entire quality workload. No double threshold.

categories.signals: weekly_hours_available is '6-8 hours' or '8+ hours', AND running_experience is 'Competitive' or the athlete already tolerates 2 quality sessions/week well
categories.structure: Same three-session skeleton, but Session 2 (support quality) can become a double-threshold day; more total threshold volume.
Two to three double-threshold sessions per week (Chapter 3's 'general load' guidance), lactate-guided.

step_1_match_athlete_to_a_category.important_note: Category is a starting point, not a cage. A recreational runner returning from a long layoff should be started BELOW their raw hours-available category (see injury_and_strength_protocol.json and the conservative-entry guidance below).

step_2_the_three_key_sessions.source: Chapter 5, section 8_weekly_structure_three_key_sessions -- 'What most often provides the best return at this level is a system built systematically around three key sessions.'

session_1_main_quality.definition: The highest-load threshold session of the week. Longer intervals (10+ min) or continuous varying-pace running for marathon-oriented athletes.
session_1_main_quality.frequency: Once per week maximum -- this session is too demanding to repeat.
session_1_main_quality.placement_rule: Needs a genuinely easy day both before and after (Chapter 3's 24-hour muscle-tone window: tone peaks the day AFTER a hard session, not during it).

session_2_support_quality.definition: Shorter threshold intervals, max duration 3 min (up to 6 min occasionally). Often takes the 45/15 form. For ambitious/elite athletes, this slot can become a double-threshold day.
session_2_support_quality.frequency: Once per week (recreational); can pair with a same-day second session for ambitious+.

session_3_x_session.definition: The flexible, variable session -- either competition-pace-specific work, or extra variation slightly above threshold. NOT mandatory.
session_3_x_session.flexibility_rule: The X-session is the first thing to cut at any sign of overload or injury -- it can also just be a normal threshold session with mild variation if the athlete needs stability instead.
session_3_x_session.placement_rule: Chapter 10's strength-training research found Model C (strength/speed work placed right after the X-session, e.g. Saturday) the best-tolerated placement -- see injury_and_strength_protocol.json.

step_2_the_three_key_sessions.everything_else: All other runs are genuinely easy (see the 70% max-HR rule in pace_and_readiness_protocol.json's related chapter-3 content). If an athlete completes only these three sessions well, with all other runs truly easy, they get steady progress -- this is the floor, not a compromise.

medium_intervals_4_to_10_min.role: The workhorse -- the default choice for session 1 or 2 for most athletes.

short_intervals_1_to_3_min.role: Higher quality, faster pace, lower lactate accumulation per rep. Good for session 2 or as part of a mixed session.
short_intervals_1_to_3_min.example: 30 x 1 min gives 30 min of threshold work distributed into manageable chunks.

long_intervals_11_to_20_min.role: Teaches stable pacing over long periods. Use sparingly -- once every 10-14 days, not weekly.
long_intervals_11_to_20_min.caution: Easy to start too hard; the second half becomes a fight against lactate instead of controlled work.
long_intervals_11_to_20_min.split_alternative: 8 min threshold, 4 min jog recovery, 8 min threshold again -- same total length, less continuous wear.

very_short_20_to_45_sec_45_15_protocol.role: A distinct category (full protocols live in Chapter 8) -- micro-intervals maximizing time-at-intensity with minimal muscular cost. Frequently used for session 2 or the X-session.

mixed_and_shaped_sessions.classic_combo: 3 x 10 min (90 sec rest) then, after a short easy jog, 10 x 45/15 -- long intervals for base load, finished with speed work.
mixed_and_shaped_sessions.pyramid: 3-6-9-6-3 min with 90 sec rest, optionally finished with 5-10 x 20/20.
mixed_and_shaped_sessions.descending: 10-8-6-4-2-1 min with increasing speed as intervals shorten.
mixed_and_shaped_sessions.pacing_rule: Start 5-7 sec/km slower than target pace on the first interval and build through the session -- soft start, soft landing. Never make the first or last interval the hardest.

continuous_threshold_efforts.role: The exception to the interval-first rule -- reserved for half-marathon/marathon-specific work: 20-40 min continuous efforts for metabolic endurance, fat oxidation, and race-pace judgment.
continuous_threshold_efforts.not_the_default: For everything shorter than a half marathon, intervals beat continuous running at the same effort -- 5-15 sec/km faster at equal load, per Chapter 3.

step_4_reference_weekly_template.source: Chapter 5, section 11_example_5_hour_week_table -- 'Example 5-Hour Week in the Base Training Period'
step_4_reference_weekly_template.note: This is a worked EXAMPLE from the book for a recreational athlete, not a rigid template -- use it as the shape to adapt, substituting the athlete's own days/paces/distances.

week.session: Support quality -- 6x6min threshold OR 10-12x3min w/ 1min recovery
Main quality -- 3-4x10min or a long varying session
Rest (or rotate if the athlete responds poorly to a fully free day before Saturday's quality)
X-session / 45/15 -- e.g. 15-20x45sec progressive (10K pace building to 5K pace) w/ 15sec rest
Long easy run -- 60-90 min for sub-10K goals, progressive week-by-week for half/full marathon goals

step_4_reference_weekly_template.cautious_entry_rule: For a returning or injury-prone athlete, keep the SAME structure but cap total threshold-session time at 20-25 minutes while they adapt, then gradually increase volume. Choose the structure first, increase volume second -- never the reverse.

models.when: Experienced athletes near the recreational/ambitious boundary, especially if weekends allow more recovery than weekdays.
models.caution: Powerful but must be done precisely -- watch the morning session closely.

models.progression_rate: About 10% volume increase per week over a 6-week block, ideally finishing ~4 weeks before a target race.

models.rule: ONLY add extra reps when the traffic-light signals (resting HR, HRV, stair test, warm-up HR -- see adaptive_progression_protocol.json) are green. Add length, not intensity.

examples: Combination: 60-90min easy directly into 45/15, no break
Step intervals: 3min broken into 1min segments, each stepping up
Active jogging rest: recovery jog kept above a HR floor instead of fully easy

step_5_how_to_increase_load_over_time.which_to_use: Individual -- the book recommends testing several over time and adopting whichever one the athlete responds to best as their fixed default strategy.
